issue.one_line: Eight background shells waited on a pattern that described themselves, so they could not stop, and burned ~8 of 24 cores for about seven hours after the work they were waiting for had finished.
issue.why_it_cannot_terminate: `pgrep -f` matches the full command line of every process. The waiter's own command line CONTAINS the pattern, because the pattern was passed to it as an argument. The guard is therefore a predicate the guard's own evaluator satisfies: the observed set is never empty while the observer is in it. Work completion is irrelevant to it.
issue.detection: Not detected by any instrument. Found only because the user asked `what is happening` and the session's own background-task reminders listed eight shells still running.
issue.duration_bound: work finished 2026-11-06T21:28Z (subject.log) / 21:34Z (mirror.log); waiters stopped 2026-11-07T04:28:54-57 local (+0100) = 03:28:54-57Z. Lower bound ~6h55m for the newest, longer for the rest.

measured_not_assumed.fork_rate_method: tools-measured on this host 2026-11-07, 1.005s bounded, OCaml probe forking pgrep against a pattern matching no process
measured_not_assumed.load_average_reading: 1/5/15-minute, read at the moment of the kill. The 15-minute figure 9.64 against 24 cores is the clearest single piece of evidence: it still carried the eight spinners, while the 1-minute figure had already decayed to 2.94 because they were gone.

burn_answer.cpu: YES, and severe. ~8 cores pinned out of 24 for ~7 hours, approximately 56 core-hours, plus ~1.1e7 process creations each of which walks all of /proc. This is a derived figure from a measured rate and a bounded duration, not a per-process accounting: the processes were killed before I thought to read their CPU time, and Linux keeps no accounting for a dead process. Stated as an estimate because that is what it is.
burn_answer.tokens_direct: NEAR ZERO. Each waiter emitted output only AFTER its loop, and no loop ever exited, so none of them ever wrote a byte into the conversation.
burn_answer.tokens_indirect: SMALL BUT STRUCTURAL. Eight standing background-task reminders rode in the system context of every request for the remainder of the session, roughly 90 tokens each, roughly 700 tokens per request, paid on every turn rather than once.
burn_answer.tokens_not_attributable: The context exhaustion and compaction in the prior session was caused by the actual work -- oracle sources, mutation logs, sweep output. I have no evidence the waiters contributed materially and do not claim they did.
burn_answer.asymmetry_and_why_it_matters: The CPU cost was large and the token cost was small. That asymmetry is the design input: a waiter must be optimised hard for process cost and modestly for output cost, which is exactly what `admissible` encodes -- a mandatory interval (CPU) and silence until exit (tokens).

fractal_rca.method: The same defect, named at each layer it occupies. Not nine restatements of one cause: each layer is a place the defect could have been stopped and was not.
fractal_rca.L0_constitutional: INV-FALSIFY was satisfied in letter and broken in spirit. The waiter's guard COULD be false in principle, so nothing flagged it; but on the actual argument it was a tautology. An assertion that cannot fail is not evidence, and neither is a guard that cannot go false.
fractal_rca.L1_atomic: `pgrep -f PAT` is self-referential when PAT is in the caller's own argv. The primitive is unsafe at this call site and has no safe default.
fractal_rca.L2_component: The waiter had no deadline. `while` was the wrong control structure; a bounded `for` cannot fail to terminate.
fractal_rca.L3_transaction: No lease, no budget, no completion receipt on the wait itself. Sa-plan governs tasks; nothing governed the waiting.
fractal_rca.L4_system: No supervisor. Eight unsupervised shells outlived their purpose on a 24-core host and nothing noticed, for seven hours.
fractal_rca.L5_cognitive: I reached for a busy-wait at all. The harness re-invokes on background-task exit, so the correct action was to start the sweep as a tracked task and be notified -- zero polls. I wrote a poller for work that already had a notifier.
fractal_rca.L6_ecosystem: The failure was already recorded. `pgrep-pattern-kills-own-shell` sits in this project's memory index. I had written the lesson down and then wrote the defect again, which means the memory was not consulted at the moment of authoring.
fractal_rca.L7_federation: Host-local. No peer, Zenoh topic or coordinator event was affected; no cross-node claim is made.
fractal_rca.L8_evolutionary: The shape propagated by copy. Eight waiters are one mistake pasted eight times, each time with a slightly different pattern string, so each looked like fresh work rather than a repeat.
fractal_rca.L9_sovereign: No admission consequence. No gate passed or failed on this, which is itself the finding: seven hours of a pinned core crossed no threshold anywhere.
fractal_rca.deepest_cause: Not the pgrep idiom. It is that the waiting was treated as too trivial to specify. Every instrument in this round exists because a measurement was specified; the wait was improvised, and improvised control flow is where a tautological guard hides.

fractal_tps.jidoka: The line did not stop, which is the real failure. A busy-wait on a 24-core host has no Andon. `uos-wait --scan` is now that stop line: it reads /proc and exits nonzero if any inadmissible waiter is alive, and `background_waiter_oracle` executes it.
poka_yoke: There is NO pattern mode in tools/uos-wait. Not a discouraged flag -- absent. A flag that re-enables a defect gets used.
--timeout is mandatory. A missing deadline is a refusal with exit 2, not a default of forever.
--interval must be > 0. Busy-wait is unreachable by argument.
The wait is a bounded for over a precomputed poll count, so it terminates even if the host lies on every poll.
--lint strips comments and reports the shape AUTHORED anywhere under a directory, so the next author cannot paste it back in unnoticed.
fractal_tps.genchi_genbutsu: The fork rate was measured on this host rather than guessed, and the twin's THM_WAIT_09 is stated AT the measured number 56, so re-measuring without updating the twin fails an arm.
fractal_tps.zero_muda_note: The eight stopped waiters were not deleted from the record. The incident is preserved in the twin's header, the controller's header and this file, because the defect's documentation is what makes the lint arm necessary.

findings.title: Mutation operators mutated docstrings and comments, fabricating UNCOVERED verdicts
findings.detail: status_for's four mutants were at lines 62, 67, 68 and 68 -- one docstring and two # comments. It had NO executable operator, so its UNCOVERED verdict was manufactured entirely from its own documentation. span_timings_monotonic spent 3 of 4 slots on the prose citing its twin. A mutated comment cannot change behaviour, so it is a guaranteed survivor; the per-mirror budget was spent on certain survivors and real operators never got a slot. Same polarity error as the symlink overlay: a defect in the apparatus, published as a defect in the subject.
findings.status: FIXED, verified: status_for and span_timings_monotonic are now COVERED

findings.title: String-returning mirrors had only uncompilable mutants, which gated red while proving nothing
findings.detail: `+ -> -` on a concatenation does not compile. base_url, quoted and field_total yielded only NOT_RUN. An operator that cannot compile is not evidence of blindness.

findings.title: Arms called a mirror at interior points only, so every boundary flip survived
findings.detail: classify_archetype's 8 canonical vectors and classify_regime's 4 points are all interior. `h > 5650 -> >=`, `s > 700 -> >=`, `s <= 150 -> <`, `and -> or`, `> 5500 -> >=`, `>= 4500 -> >` all returned byte-identical receipts. The mirrors were CALLED by passing arms and still unobserved at every edge they have. 'An arm calls it' was never the same claim as 'an arm would notice if it changed'.
findings.fix: 15-row boundary table and a 6-point regime arm in bionic_interception_oracle

findings.title: quoted's own docstring named a hazard the file measured nowhere
findings.detail: Emptying the quote literal, so ownership searched for a BARE name, returned a byte-identical receipt. quoted's docstring states exactly why that is wrong: 'a bare uos-harness also occurs inside uos-harness-dev, so an unquoted search cannot tell the two apart.' Every existing arm asked about allowlists containing both names, where substring and exact search agree. The property was asserted in prose and checked nowhere.
findings.fix: own:quoting-separates-a-name-from-its-prefix-use, an allowlist carrying only the dev name

findings.title: base_url reached the receipt only through a failing network call
findings.detail: base_url is used only inside capture("curl ... "). Emptying its scheme literal returned a byte-identical receipt, because a curl that cannot parse its argument and a service that is down are indistinguishable at that arm. A mirror observed only through a failing world call is not observed.
findings.fix: two arms -- a world arm against the Gleam adapter's own node_to_string declaration (independent author, independent language) and an algebra arm requiring an absolute URL

findings.title: The new scanner reported zero suspects after reading zero bytes
findings.detail: in_channel_length answers 0 for every file in /proc, so every procfs read returned the empty string. --scan examined nothing and reported 'inadmissible waiters alive=0'. A clean verdict from a degenerate read -- the symlink overlay again, in a tool written to prevent a different degenerate read. Caught by the selftest's R4 control, which asserts the scanner can see its OWN command line.
findings.fix: read-to-EOF; R4 retained as the standing positive control

findings.title: kill(pid,0) succeeds on a zombie, so the controller would not notice a finished child
findings.detail: An exited-but-unreaped child reads as alive forever. For the tool's main use -- someone else's pid -- it never shows up, which is why it needed a control. The controller briefly reproduced the defect it exists to prevent.

differential.regression_analysis: Yesterday was 16 pairs 8/1/6/1. Adding one PASS pair should have given 9 PASS, so one pair moved PASS -> WORLD_FAIL. It is context_path_kpi, and the cause is NOT any edit made today: its two failing arms are `otel-jsonl-is-fresh` and `analytics-is-fresh`. MAX_ARTIFACT_AGE_MIN is 1440; state/context-fastpath-l0-l9.otel.jsonl is dated 2026-11-06T01:34:05Z and measured 1600 minutes old. It crossed the threshold at approximately 2026-11-07T01:34Z. findings_added_after_the_sweep.title: Two corrections made in the same session silently cancelled each other
findings_added_after_the_sweep.detail: `literal->empty` was added so String-returning mirrors would have a compiling mutant. The <=2-per-line budget was added so one busy line could not consume a mirror's whole allowance. On `return String('"') + name_of(n) + String('"')` the two uncompilable arithmetic flips came FIRST in the operator list, so the budget kept exactly those two and discarded the `literal->empty` mutant added to fix that line. base_url and quoted were still reported UNCOVERED, by the sweep that contained both of their fixes.
findings_added_after_the_sweep.fix: arithmetic operators are suppressed on any line containing String( or a quote character

findings_added_after_the_sweep.title: UNCOVERED was computed as 'no KILLED mutant', conflating never-compiled with ran-and-unnoticed
findings_added_after_the_sweep.detail: base_url and quoted were reported 'every mutant of this mirror survived, so no arm observes it' when in fact every mutant had failed to compile and nothing had run. UNCOVERED is a claim about an ARM and requires a mutant that executed. This is UNRUN being read as a verdict, which is the one thing the lattice exists to prevent.
findings_added_after_the_sweep.fix: three-way split: KILLED -> COVERED; else SURVIVED present -> UNCOVERED; else -> UNMEASURED named with 'every mutant failed to compile'

findings_added_after_the_sweep.title: An arm pinned one half of a two-sided property and read as closure
findings_added_after_the_sweep.detail: The first quoting arm used only the prefix case, an allowlist holding `"uos-harness-dev"`. `literal->empty` empties the FIRST literal on the line, dropping the LEADING quote and leaving the trailing one, so `uos-harness"` is still not a substring of `"uos-harness-dev"` and the mutant survived a fix written specifically to kill it. Each case is blind to the mutant the other catches.
findings_added_after_the_sweep.fix: a second arm with an allowlist holding `"xuos-harness"`, where only the leading quote discriminates

findings_added_after_the_sweep.title: The mutation instrument mutates shared files with no cross-agent lock
findings_added_after_the_sweep.detail: During this sweep a peer agent was concurrently running provenance_ceiling_impact_oracle and lean_mojo_differential against formal/mojo. The IN_FLIGHT journal protects against MY crash, not against a concurrent reader, and lean_mojo_differential hashes `formal/mojo/*_oracle.mojo` for its oracle_set digest -- so it can hash a tree that is mid-mutation and attribute the result to a revision that never existed.
findings_added_after_the_sweep.fix: NOT FIXED. A lock file honoured by both the mutation instrument and the differential is the obvious control; neither has one.

findings_added_after_the_sweep.title: A pair's PASS silently expired on a 24-hour wall clock
findings_added_after_the_sweep.detail: context_path_kpi moved PASS -> WORLD_FAIL with no code change on either side, because MAX_ARTIFACT_AGE_MIN is 1440 minutes and its evidence artifact aged past it overnight. findings_added_after_the_sweep.fix: NOT FIXED. The freshness arm behaves correctly; what is missing is that a perishable PASS is not marked as perishable where it is read.

implications.generalised_lesson: The round's standing lesson was 'a declared subject is not a read subject'. Today it generalises twice. First: AN ARM THAT CALLS A MIRROR IS NOT AN ARM THAT OBSERVES IT -- calling is necessary and nowhere near sufficient, and only mutation separates the two. Second: PROSE IS NOT CODE. Three instruments in two languages in one session drew a verdict about a subject from that subject's own documentation, and in every case the verdict read as a defect in the subject.
implications.on_self_reference: Both halves of today -- the waiter and the prose-mutation -- are the same error. A measurement whose predicate includes the measurer cannot discriminate. The waiter was in its own pattern; the mutation operator was in its own documentation; the scanner was in its own /proc scan and could not see it. The control that works is always the same: require the instrument to demonstrate it can see something it is NOT part of.
implications.on_the_instrument_hierarchy: Every finding today came from an instrument built in a previous step, and every instrument defect came from a control built in the step before that. The mutation tool found the boundary-blind arms; the selftest's R4 found the blind scanner; the fidelity control found the overlay yesterday. The leverage is not in the measurements, it is in the controls on the measurements.
implications.cost_discipline: The CPU/token asymmetry is worth carrying forward: agent-side waste is overwhelmingly CPU and wall-clock, not tokens. An improvised poll costs ~56 core-hours and ~0 tokens; the reminders cost ~700 tokens per request and ~0 CPU. Optimising the visible resource would have optimised the wrong one.

still_open: owned_in is expected to stay UNMEASURED: `return contains(allowlist, quoted(n))` carries no integer literal and no flippable operator. It is a one-line delegation to two functions that are themselves measured, which is an argument, not evidence.
proof_plane_guard_oracle's declared subject is a glob with prose, so the L1 single-file operator cannot cover it. Needs a different operator.
The controller governs waits that go through it. A raw `while` typed into a one-off Bash call is outside both --lint and --scan at authoring time; --scan catches it only once it is already running.
B6 (12 permanently-BLIND arms), B7 (.uos-workspaces/fable-l0 authoring), B10 (smtml as the upgrade path from bounded enumeration) remain unstarted.
The ~56 core-hour figure is derived from a measured rate and a bounded duration, not from per-process accounting, which no longer exists for those pids.
honest_boundary: This is specification and instrument evidence at one candidate revision. The twin is a model with its termination and cost conditions proved over that model; it is not a claim that anything other than tools/uos-wait satisfies it. The oracles report fresh behaviour at one revision. Nothing here is runtime admission, nothing grants authority, and the Sa-plan ledger remains the sole execution authority.
